security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are Markdown backticks or examples, not Ruby shell backtick execution. The skill still depends on infsh and inference.sh, and it allows broad infsh command execution plus remote rendering of user-provided TSX. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed-tools to the minimum rendering command and require confirmation for login or unrelated account operations.

remediation.issue: User TSX code and props are sent to inference.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy warning telling users not to include secrets, proprietary code, or regulated data in render inputs.

remediation.issue: Documentation recommends installing additional skills with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Move related skill install commands behind explicit user confirmation and explain the supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: The README loads an image from cloud.inference.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Use a bundled marketplace-safe image or state that viewing the README loads a third-party asset.

content.value_statement: Rendering Remotion animations can require local setup and build tooling. This skill sends component code to inference.sh and returns an MP4 render.
actual_capabilities: Runs the inference.sh remotion-render app with TSX component input.
Renders MP4 video from React and Remotion component code.
Supports width, height, FPS, duration, and codec settings.
Passes props into rendered components for reusable templates.
Uses Remotion APIs such as useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, and Sequence.
Shows CLI and Python SDK workflows, including streaming progress.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated inference.sh CLI or Python SDK.
Sends component code and props to an external rendering service.
Does not inspect or guarantee the security of submitted TSX code.
Requires the code to export a default Remotion component.

use_cases.title: Create Branded Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Render reusable Remotion title cards, logo animations, and short visual assets as MP4 files.

use_cases.title: Generate Data Video Assets
use_cases.description: Use props and component logic to produce charts, counters, and metric videos from structured inputs.

use_cases.title: Automate Product Videos
use_cases.description: Turn repeatable React video templates into rendered clips for releases, demos, and social channels.

prompt_templates.title: Render A Simple Intro
prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-render to create a 3-second 1080p fade-in title video with a dark background and centered text.

prompt_templates.title: Render With Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a 5-second square Remotion video that accepts title and subtitle props for a social media announcement.

prompt_templates.title: Render A Sequence Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create and render a 4-second Remotion sequence with three timed text sections and smooth fade transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Progress Reporting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python SDK workflow to render a 10-second dashboard animation and report streaming progress until the MP4 is ready.

output_examples.input: A request to render a three second fade-in title at 1920 by 1080.
output_examples.output: An MP4 render link from inference.sh with the title fading in over the requested duration.

output_examples.input: A square animated counter for a social media post.
output: The counter increases across the full duration.
The result is ready for download or sharing.

output_examples.input: A product update video using title and subtitle props.
output_examples.output: A short MP4 clip that applies the supplied text values to the Remotion template.

best_practices: Remove secrets, customer data, and private source code before submitting render inputs.
Set duration, FPS, and resolution explicitly so the render output is predictable.
Preview short or low-resolution versions before rendering long production videos.
anti_patterns: Submitting confidential code or regulated data inside TSX strings or props.
Using broad infsh commands that are unrelated to the remotion-render app.
Rendering long high-resolution videos before validating timing and layout.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion component code into MP4 video through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require local Remotion setup?
faq.answer: No local Remotion project is shown, but the inference.sh CLI or SDK must be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can I pass dynamic text or data?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented props input lets a component receive values at render time.

faq.question: Where does my code run?
faq.answer: The documented workflow sends the render input to the inference.sh remotion-render app.

faq.question: Which Remotion APIs are supported?
faq.answer: The skill documents useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, interpolate, AbsoluteFill, and Sequence.

faq.question: Should I include secrets in the input?
faq.answer: No. Do not submit secrets, private code, or sensitive customer data in component code or props.
